investigation.method: manual review of the live website with NHS profile and search-result cross-checks

headline: Charlestown looks like a messier transition case than the standard GTD microsites. The public site is a WordPress and Silicon Practice build, the direct request form points to PATCHS, but the NHS App wording still says continue to the Accurx system, and prescriptions still mention Patient Access.

live_stack.label: Public website stack
live_stack.platform: WordPress with NHS UK theme and Silicon Practice elements
evidence: The site exposes WordPress and wp-content assets.
The page source carries Silicon Practice markers.

live_stack.label: Direct online request platform
evidence: The page presents PATCHS as the direct online request form.

live_stack.label: NHS App wording still visible on the site
evidence: The appointments page tells NHS App users to continue to the accurx system.

live_stack.label: Prescription-side legacy platform
evidence: The prescriptions page says repeat prescriptions can be ordered using the GP online system: Patient Access.

current_routes.label: PATCHS direct route
notes: The appointments page presents PATCHS as the direct online request form.
The page also says appointment outcomes may be by phone, face to face, video call, text or email.

current_routes.label: NHS App route
notes: The NHS App instructions still say continue to the accurx system.
Treat that as website wording rather than a fully trusted statement of the current stack.

current_routes.label: Phone route
current_routes.kind: staff-assisted intake, not a distinct digital platform
notes: The page lists phoning the practice as another way to request an appointment.

current_routes.label: Prescriptions
notes: The prescriptions page points patients to NHS account and Patient Access.
It says repeat requests are not taken over the phone or email.
It also says nominated pharmacy changes can be handled at the surgery or online via PATCHS.

complaints_and_feedback.headline: Charlestown has a live dedicated complaints page, but it reads like a generic complaints procedure rather than the clearer GTD contact-us model used on the concrete microsites.

items.label: Dedicated complaints page
notes: The page gives a generic complaints procedure and says patients can phone the practice or visit the surgery to raise issues.
No GTD complaints-team contact details were obvious during this pass.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: PATCHS vs Accurx wording
notes: The direct online request route is PATCHS, but the NHS App instructions still point to Accurx.

stale_or_conflicting_signals.label: Multiple prescription-era systems remain visible
notes: The prescriptions page still mentions Patient Access while also referencing PATCHS for nominated pharmacy changes.

probably_true: PATCHS is probably the current direct patient request platform.
Charlestown is still exposing more legacy and mixed-system language than the standard GTD microsites.
needs_follow_up: Whether the NHS App genuinely still hands Charlestown requests to Accurx or whether that wording is just stale.
Whether Patient Access is still operational for repeat prescriptions here or simply left in the copy.
